conclusion: The earlier gzip EOF failure was an engineering defect in the F20-M2 health checker, not evidence of damaged F20-M1 capture. The repaired monitor passed on the live collector with all 30 active tokens structurally recent.

incident.description: Health checker could attempt to read a gzip file that was still open by the live F20-M1 collector. The previous logic excluded only the current wall-clock minute, while the MinuteGzipWriter may legitimately keep a previous-minute stream file open until that stream next writes.

repair.mechanic: Discover gzip paths actually held open by the live rn1-f20-m1-clob.service MainPID through /proc/<PID>/fd and exclude those paths from completed-file inspection. Retain current-minute exclusion as an additional safeguard.
